texts.facts: 1. The present claim arises out of a detailed accident report (Dar), filed by the police qua injuries suffered by one Suminder Singh (aged 26 years) in a road traffic accident. 2. The brief facts of the case are that on 21.02.2016 at about 09:15 p.m. victim was returning home after completing his duty at Holy Family Hospital. When he reached near the gate of Delhi Jal board for taxi, suddenly a motorcycle bearing no. Suminder Singh vs Samir (6316 Nfc) on 30 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147308600/ 1 DL-3SBG-0762 (hereinafter referred as the offending vehicle) came in a rash and negligent manner and hit the victim. Due to the impact, victim sustained grievous injury in his left leg. Victim was taken to Holy Family Hospital for treatment. 3. An FIR no.0063/16 dated 22.02.2016 was registered u/s 279, 337 IPC at PS New Friends Colony and the matter was investigated. After investigation, chargesheet was filed u/s 379/338 of IPC and Section 3/181 of MV Act before concerned criminal court against the driver of the offending vehicle while DAR was filed before this Tribunal. 4. Respondent no.1 is driver of offending vehicle while respondent no.2 is the owner. The offending vehicle was not insured at the time of accident. 5. Despite opportunity, respondent no.1 failed to file his reply. His defence was struck off vide order dated 17.11.2016. Page no. 2 of 18 ss CHARU by CHARU GUPTA Even the owner of the vehicle failed to appeare despite service of process and was accordingly proceeded ex-parte vide order dated 17.11.2016. 6. Vide order dated 29.01.2018, following issues were framed: 1. Whether the injured Sh. Suminder Singh suffered injures in a road traffic accident dated 21.02.2016 involving vehicle bearing no. DL-3SBG-0762 driven by R1 and owned by R2 and not insured (inadvertently written as insured with R3).?OPP 2. Whether the claimant is entitled to any compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom? OPP 3. Relief. 7. In order to prove his case, petitioner examined himself as PW-1 wherein he tendered his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW-1/1. He deposed that on 21.02.2016 he was coming on foot after completing his duties of housekeeping from the Holy Family Hospital. At about 09:15 p.m., when he reached the gate of Delhi Jal Board for taxi, suddenly a motorcycle came from font, in a rash and negligent manner and hit the victim. Due to this he fell down on the road. His friend namely Vinod reached at the spot and removed him to the hospital for medical treatment. He further deposed that he remained in the hospital from 21.02.2016 to 25.02.2016. He sustained fracture in both of his left legs and testified to have expended more than Rs.60,000/- on his treatment. He further deposed that he was working as a housekeeping staff at Holy Family Hospital and was earning of Rs.10250/- per month. He relied upon his MLC as Ex.PW1/A, Discharge MACT No: 4037/16 Suminder Singh vs. Samir & anr. Page no. 3 of 18 ss CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date: Suminder Singh vs Samir (6316 Nfc) on 30 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147308600/ 2 2025.04.30 16:13:13 +0530 summary as Ex.PW1/B, Medical bills as Ex.PW1/C, DAR as Ex.PW1/D, his salary slip for the month of February 2016 as Ex.PW1/E and Adhar Card as Ex.PW1/F. He was not cross examined by respondents despite opportunity. 8. No evidence was led by the respondent no.1 despite opportunity. 9. Final arguments in detail were addressed on behalf of both the parties. 10. It is the contention of the petitioner that the accident has been duly proved to have taken place due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1. The petitioner was 26 years of age and working as housekeeper at Holy Family Hospital. He was earning Rs.10,250/-p.m. It has been prayed that an Award as per the entitlement be passed by the Tribunal. Respondent side shall also furnish TDS certificate, if any to the petitioner. Since, the present case was adjourned sine die for failure by the petitioner to lead evidence and was subsequently restored vide order dated 10.05.2024, petitioner is not entitled to interest from dated 05.09.2018 till date of restoration on 10.05.2024.
texts.arguments: On the other hand, it is argued on behalf of respondents that the accident did not occurr due to the negligence of respondent no.1. It is argued that the treatment record is manupulated as the petitioner worked in the same hospital from where such record has been procured. Reliance is placed upon decision in Bimla Devi & ors. vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & ors. (2009) 13 SC 535, in Parmeshwari vs. Amir Chand & ors., 2011 (1) SCR 1096 and National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana, 2009 ACJ 287, wherein it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view has to be taken. In National Insurance Co. vs. MACT No: 4037/16 Suminder Singh vs. Samir & anr. Page no. 5 of 18 ss CHARU by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.04.30 16:13:19 +0530 Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of chargesheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 16. It may further be noted that in Cholamandalam Insurance Company vs. Kamlesh, 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it was held that if the driver of the offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. 19. Now as regards the issue of quantum of compensation, this court relies upon the judgments of C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T. Kunhikuttan Nair, R.D. Hattangadi v. Pest Control (India) (P) Ltd. and Baker v. Willoughby which are referred and relied in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343 decided by Hon'ble SC wherein it has been observed that the provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which Suminder Singh vs Samir (6316 Nfc) on 30 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147308600/ 4 means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. 20.6. It was observed by Apex Court in such case of Raj Kumar (supra) that what usually poses some difficulty is the assessment of the loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability --Item (ii) (a). 20.7. 24. Having regard to the prevailing rate of interest and the judgments of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, including in the case of Erudhaya Priya vs State Express Transport decided on 27 July, 2020, Civil Appeal Nos. 2811-2812 OF 2020 [Arising out of SLP (C) Nos.8495-8496 of 2018], which is three Judges Bench judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court, such interest @ 7.5% per annum is deemed fit and accordingly granted in the present case. ......In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation".
